docs.title: DeeZy
docs.text:
A compact, portable audio encoding tool built around the Dolby Encoding Engine (DEE) 6.7 command-line tools. This documentation site collects installation instructions, configuration details, usage examples, and troubleshooting help.

Quick links

  • Installation: Installation page
  • Configuration: Configuration page
  • Usage and CLI: Usage page
  • Examples & Workflows: Examples page
  • Reference: Reference page
  • Troubleshooting: Troubleshooting page

docs.title: Batch & Retention
docs.text:
When --batch-summary-output is enabled, DeeZy writes a JSON summary per batch containing batch_info and results array.

batch_info includes: timestamp, command, total_files, successful, failed, skipped, processing, total_duration_seconds, max_parallel.

Each results entry includes: input_file, output_file, log_file, status, file_id, start_time, end_time, duration_seconds, error.

Retention

  • --max-logs and --max-batch-results control how many files are kept in working dir.

A sample file is available at docs/sample_batch_results.json in the repository.

docs.title: Bitrates
docs.text:
deezy bitrates lists, for each format and mode, every layout's default data rate and every rate DEE takes for it, in kbps. Each format's page has the same list.

deezy bitrates
deezy bitrates ddp ddp-atmos
  • An integer --bitrate picks a total rate. One DEE doesn't take becomes the closest one it does, with a warning.
  • [default_bitrates] in the config changes a default, and deezy bitrates shows it beside DeeZy's own. [default_source_bitrates] sets a default per source channel count.
  • A layout marked "needs dee_shim" is encoded through dee_shim.
  • TrueHD (thd, thd-atmos) is lossless and has no data rate.

docs.title: Substream bitrates
docs.text:
deezy encode ddp-atmos --atmos-mode standard --bitrate 1024:512 input.mkv

This requests 1024 kbps for the independent stream and 512 kbps for the dependent stream, or 1536 kbps total. With dee_shim, exact pairs work for DD+ 7.0 and 7.1, DD+ Blu-ray 7.0 and 7.1, and the standard and Blu-ray DD+ Atmos modes. Each E-AC-3 stream takes 32 to 1024 kbps. For Blu-ray the first value is the AC-3 core rate, one of 224, 256, 320, 384, 448, 512, 576 or 640 kbps. A low rate can leave too little room for the source metadata.

Use the same option in presets. To make the example your default, set standard = "1024:512" under [default_bitrates.ddp-atmos]. The other keys that accept pairs are bluray in that section and surroundex under [default_bitrates.ddp] and [default_bitrates.ddp-bluray].

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
DeeZy uses a TOML-based configuration file (deezy-conf.toml) to provide sensible defaults and reusable presets. CLI arguments always override config values.

Key sections

  • [dependencies] — paths to the tools: ffmpeg, dee (the DEE 6.7 tools' folder), truehdd and dee_shim
  • [global_defaults] — defaults for the options of every command (see below), and DeeZy's own settings such as working_dir and max_logs
  • [default_bitrates] — default data rates, one section per format, such as [default_bitrates.ddp-atmos]
  • [presets] — named command strings for common workflows

Quick commands

deezy config generate
deezy config info
deezy --config my-config.toml encode ddp input.mkv

Example snippets

[dependencies]
ffmpeg = ""
dee = ""
truehdd = ""
dee_shim = ""

[global_defaults]
keep_temp = false
max_parallel = 1
allow_sleep = false
overwrite = false

[presets]
streaming_ddp = "encode ddp --channels surround --bitrate 448"

docs.title: Global defaults
docs.text:
A [global_defaults] key is an option's name with _ for -, and its value is that option's default:

[global_defaults]
speech_threshold = 20       # --speech-threshold 20
drc_line_mode = "music_light"
lt_rt_center = "-1.5"
keep_temp = true            # --keep-temp
dialogue_intelligence = false
  • A --no-x switch takes either name: dialogue_intelligence = false and no_dialogue_intelligence = true both turn dialogue intelligence off.
  • A key applies to every command that has the option, so drc_line_mode changes dd, ddp, ddp-bluray and ddp-atmos and nothing else.
  • The command line and a preset still win.
  • A key that names no option, or a value the option refuses, is ignored with a warning.
  • bitrate goes under [default_bitrates], and the tools' paths under [dependencies].

Per-source default bitrates are opt-in via [default_source_bitrates.<codec>] and allow pick-by-channel-count.

deezy bitrates shows the defaults a config changes beside DeeZy's own.

docs.title: Sections from DeeZy 1.x
docs.text:
DeeZy 2.0 renamed two formats, so two 1.x sections are ignored, with a warning:

  • [default_bitrates.atmos] is now [default_bitrates.ddp-atmos].
  • 1.x's [default_bitrates.ac4] was immersive stereo, which is now [default_bitrates.ac4-ims]; ac4 is now channel-based AC-4. DeeZy warns when an ac4 section has immersive stereo keys.

The same goes for [default_source_bitrates].

docs.title: dee_shim
docs.text: dee_shim is an optional tool that runs DEE's encoders with options they don't offer on their own. DeeZy works without it, but some encodes need it, and DeeZy runs others through it when it is there. DeeZy's executables don't include it.

docs.title: What needs it
docs.text: Encode Without dee_shim ddp 7.1 or 7.0 (--channels 8, or a 7.0 source) --channels 8 is refused; auto picks 5.1, a 7.0 source becomes 5.0 ddp-bluray from a 7.0 source coded as 7.1 with a silent LFE ddp-atmos --atmos-mode standard or bluray refused --bitrate R0:R1 for two-substream DD+ or DD+ Atmos refused ddp-atmos --no-surround-90-deg-phase-shift refused thd or thd-atmos with --drc none refused thd --layout 5.1.2 refused deezy measure of a 7.1 or 7-channel source refused

docs.title: What runs through it
docs.text:
When DeeZy finds dee_shim, every ddp-atmos, thd and thd-atmos encode runs through it. On AMD Zen CPUs these encodes run several times faster. The output changes in three places, each with an option that keeps plain DEE's:

  • ddp-atmos codes the master's object metadata as it is, where DEE would smooth it. --no-oamd-as-is keeps DEE's smoothing.
  • thd at 96 kHz has no apodizing filter, so it decodes to the source sample for sample. --no-as-is keeps the filter.
  • thd-atmos codes a master of no more elements than --atmos-elements as it is, so it decodes to it sample for sample. --no-as-is keeps DEE's processing.

Channel-based DD+ uses dee_shim for 7.0, standard 7.1, and Blu-ray 7.1 with a split bitrate. deezy measure uses it only for 7.1: DEE's meter has 7.1, but its command line takes 1.0, 2.0 and 5.1 only.

docs.title: How DeeZy finds it
docs.text:
DeeZy needs dee_shim 0.3.0 or newer. It takes, in order:

  1. --dee-shim PATH;
  2. dee_shim in the config's [dependencies];
  3. dee_shim beside the DEE tools;
  4. apps/dee_shim/ beside DeeZy;
  5. dee_shim on PATH.

An older dee_shim that DeeZy finds is skipped; an older one you give fails the encode. --no-shim, or no_shim = true in the config's [global_defaults], turns dee_shim off. deezy tools shows the dee_shim DeeZy would use.

docs.title: Delay
docs.text:
How is delay handled?

  • If delay is detected inside a container (mkv, mp4, etc and it includes a video track) there can be a delay relative to source field. DeeZy will utilize this to automatically detect and strip the delay to 0 for the output.
  • If there is a delay string in the filename, it will strip the delay to 0 for the output.
  • CLI argument --delay=10ms overrides all above detection if utilized. It takes milliseconds or seconds, decimals allowed, or frames at a frame rate: --delay=-10.5ms, --delay=1.25s, --delay=-3@23.976 (the rate may also be 24000/1001, ntsc, pal, film or ntsc-film). The = is required for a negative value.
  • If provided it will pad/trim Nms from the file to essentially set it to 0.

When does delay stripping take place?

DeeZy feeds the appropriate parameters to DEE during encoding to strip the delay.

What happens to the delay string in my filename?

If DeeZy strips the delay it will output DELAY 0ms to the output file name (if automatically generating the filename).

Notes

  • Filename modifications will only happen for automatically generated names via the template or by the user providing no output. Filename modifications will not happen if a user explicitly sets the filename.
  • Delay detection is always ran.
  • Priority is CLI > container > filename.

docs.title: Dynamic Range Compression (DRC)
docs.text:
The DRC profiles are film_standard, film_light (the default), music_standard, music_light, speech and none (no compression).

Format Options dd, ddp, ddp-bluray, ddp-atmos --drc-line-mode, --drc-rf-mode ac4, ac4-atmos --flat-panel-drc, --home-theatre-drc, --portable-headphones-drc, --portable-speakers-drc ac4-ims the four AC-4 device options and --ddp-drc thd, thd-atmos --drc, for every presentation in the stream

Channel-based AC-4 (ac4) has no none profile, and TrueHD's none needs dee_shim. AAC has no DRC options.

deezy encode ddp --drc-line-mode film_light --drc-rf-mode music_light input.mkv
deezy encode thd --drc music_light input.mkv

docs.title: Examples & Workflows
docs.text:
Movie encoding

deezy config generate
deezy info "Movie.Name.2023.UHD.mkv"
deezy encode preset --name bluray_atmos "Movie.Name.2023.UHD.mkv"

Batch TV series

deezy find "TV.Series.S01**/*.mkv"
deezy encode preset --name streaming_ddp "TV.Series.S01**/*.mkv"

Quality control and debugging

deezy --log-to-file encode ddp --keep-temp input.mkv
deezy temp clean --dry-run

docs.title: File Management & Analysis
docs.text:
Find files

deezy find "**/*.mkv"
deezy find -n "**/*.mkv"

Analyze streams

deezy info input.mkv
deezy info *.mkv

Track numbering in info maps to audio track selection behavior.

docs.title: Input Types & Patterns
docs.text:
Multiple files and glob patterns are supported.

Important

Use quotes if paths contain spaces

Example: "/some_path/sub path/example.mkv"

docs.title: Single Input
docs.text: deezy encode ddp "/media/input one.mkv"

docs.title: Multiple Input
docs.text: deezy encode ddp input1.mkv "/media/input 2.mp4" input3.aac

docs.title: Recursive Input (Single Folder)
docs.text:
Iterate a single folder for mkv files.

deezy encode dd "/media/path one/*.mkv"

docs.title: Recursive Input (Multiple Folders)
docs.text:
Iterate multiple folders for aac files.

deezy encode dd "/media/path two/**/*.aac"

docs.title: Recursive Input (Multiple Folders Advanced)
docs.text:
Iterate two different directories for media files files.

deezy encode dd "/media/path two/**/*.aac" "/media/path three/**/*.mkv"

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: DeeZy needs FFmpeg and the DEE 6.7 command-line tools. truehdd is needed for TrueHD Atmos sources, and dee_shim is optional.

docs.title: DeeZy
docs.text:
Download an executable from the releases page, or install the Python package:

pipx install deezy

The executable comes in two builds:

  • Bundled: the executable has a bundle/ folder beside it, so it unpacks once. Best for a PATH install or for calling DeeZy from other programs.
  • Standalone: a single executable that unpacks on demand, which can mean every run.

For a development install from a checkout, use pipx install --editable ..

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Tool Needed for FFmpeg every encode DEE 6.7 command-line tools every encode truehdd a TrueHD Atmos source for ddp-atmos, thd-atmos, ac4-atmos or ac4-ims, which it decodes; an Atmos master (DAMF or ADM BWF) doesn't need it. DeeZy is tested with truehdd 0.6.3 dee_shim 0.3.0 or newer optional; see dee_shim

DEE 6.7 is a folder of command-line tools, one per job (dee_ddp_encoder, dee_ddpjoc_encoder, dee_dthd_encoder, dee_ac4_encoder, dee_ac4ims_encoder, dee_ac4ajoc_encoder, dee_aac_encoder, dee_measure_loudness and others). Keep the folder whole: the tools need the mediainfo.dll beside them. DeeZy refuses any other DEE version, including the single dee executable of DEE 5.2 that DeeZy 1.x used; see Migrating from 1.x.

docs.title: Where DeeZy finds the tools
docs.text:
For each tool DeeZy takes, in order:

  1. the path given with --ffmpeg, --dee, --truehdd or --dee-shim;
  2. the path under [dependencies] in the config;
  3. the apps folder beside DeeZy;
  4. PATH.

On Windows DeeZy also finds the DEE tools of an installed Dolby Media Encoder. --dee takes the tools' folder, or the path of one of them. The portable layout is:

deezy.exe
└── apps/
    ├── ffmpeg/ffmpeg.exe
    ├── dee/            # the DEE 6.7 tools, with mediainfo.dll
    ├── truehdd/truehdd.exe
    └── dee_shim/dee_shim.exe   # optional

docs.title: DEE license
docs.text: The DEE tools look for a license.lic beside themselves. When there isn't one, DeeZy passes them a Dolby Media Encoder license: dme_license.lic beside the tools, or license.lic in %APPDATA%\Dolby Media Encoder. The license must cover DEE 6.7.

docs.title: Check the setup
docs.text:
deezy tools shows the FFmpeg, DEE tools, truehdd and dee_shim an encode would use, with each one's version and path, and the license the DEE tools get. It exits with 1 when an encode couldn't run.

deezy tools

docs.title: Migrating from DeeZy 1.x
docs.text:
DeeZy 2.0 runs only the DEE 6.7 command-line tools. The single dee of DEE 5.2 and other DEE versions are refused. See Installation, and check the setup with deezy tools.

The changes most likely to affect your commands, presets and config come first.

docs.title: 1. Renamed formats, and what ac4 means now
docs.text:
1.x 2.0 atmos ddp-atmos ac4 (immersive stereo) ac4-ims ac4: channel-based AC-4, 2.0 or 5.1
  • A 1.x atmos command or preset fails: atmos is no longer a format.
  • A 1.x ac4 command still runs, but it now makes channel-based AC-4 instead of immersive stereo. DeeZy logs a notice each time ac4 runs. Change ac4 to ac4-ims to keep 1.x's output. Options only immersive stereo takes, such as --encoding-profile, make an ac4 command fail.
  • In the config, [default_bitrates.atmos] is now [default_bitrates.ddp-atmos], and 1.x's [default_bitrates.ac4] is now [default_bitrates.ac4-ims]. DeeZy ignores the 1.x sections and warns about them. The same goes for [default_source_bitrates].

docs.title: 2. Surround 3 dB attenuation is off by default
docs.text: DeeZy 1.x lowered the surround channels of dd, ddp and ddp-bluray by 3 dB. DeeZy 2.0 follows DEE's default and leaves them alone. --surround-3db turns the attenuation on and gives 1.x's output. --no-surround-3db still parses and asks for what is now the default.

docs.title: 3. Warp mode for a TrueHD Atmos stream that has none
docs.text: DeeZy 1.x gave such a stream the normal warp mode when it decoded it with truehdd. DeeZy 2.0 gives it none, so DEE renders it as warping, its own default. This changes ddp-atmos, ac4-atmos and ac4-ims encodes of such a stream; thd-atmos audio doesn't change. --thd-warp-mode normal gives 1.x's output. A stream that has a warp mode keeps it.

docs.title: 4. Loudness and data rate defaults
docs.text:
These are unchanged: DEE measures the loudness and writes the measured dialnorm (measure_only), and DeeZy keeps its own default rates, which are higher than DEE's automatic ones. What changed:

  • The rates each format takes are DEE 6.7's, listed by deezy bitrates. A rate DEE doesn't take becomes the closest one it does, with a warning.
  • --metering-mode is gone: DEE 6.7 measures with ITU-R BS.1770-4 only. Remove it from commands and presets.
  • The new aac format leaves the loudness as it is by default, because DEE's AAC encoder can't only measure it.

docs.title: 5. --bed-conform is gone
docs.text: It changed no DEE output. Remove it from commands and presets; DeeZy refuses it.

docs.title: 6. [global_defaults] keys now apply
docs.text: DeeZy 1.x ignored the option keys under [global_defaults], such as speech_threshold, drc_line_mode, stereo_down_mix, track_index and keep_temp. DeeZy 2.0 makes each the default of its option (see Configuration). A config made by 1.x's deezy config generate has speech_threshold = 20, which now applies: DeeZy's own default is 15. Delete the line or set it to 15 to keep 1.x's output. A key that names no option, such as metering_mode, is ignored with a warning.

docs.title: Other removed options
docs.text:
• --ims-legacy-presentation (1.5.0 already ignored it).
  • --metering-mode (see 4).

docs.title: Layouts
docs.text:
• A 5.0 source to dd or ddp is coded as 5.0; 1.x downmixed it to 2.0. --upmix-50-to-51 still gives 5.1 with a silent LFE.
  • A 7.0 source: ddp codes 7.0 through dee_shim, else 5.0; ddp-bluray codes 7.0 through dee_shim, else 7.1 with a silent LFE (1.x refused it).
  • DD+ 7.1 (ddp --channels 8) works through dee_shim, at 384 to 1792 kbps. With --channels 0, an 8-channel source gets 7.1 when DeeZy has dee_shim, else 5.1 with a notice.

docs.title: ddp-atmos
docs.text:
• --atmos-mode bluray now codes a 7.1 backbone with an AC-3 core (1152 to 1664 kbps) and needs dee_shim. DEE's own Blu-ray mode, which 1.x used, gives a 5.1.2 backbone.
  • --atmos-mode standard is new: a 7.1 backbone as E-AC-3, 448 to 2048 kbps, 1152 by default. It needs dee_shim.
  • Through dee_shim, every ddp-atmos encode codes the master's object metadata as it is. --no-oamd-as-is gives plain DEE's output.
  • --no-surround-90-deg-phase-shift now works for ddp-atmos, through dee_shim.

docs.title: Blu-ray secondary audio
docs.text: ddp --bluray-secondary takes 96 to 256 kbps for 2.0 and 160 to 256 kbps for 5.1 (1.5.0 took 192 or 256). A rate it doesn't take becomes the closest one.

docs.title: Output names and files
docs.text:
• The automatic name of a single input has no _f1.
  • An output template drops an empty [] or () left by a field with no value, so {title} [{lang}] with no language gives title.ec3.
  • {stem-cleaned} works; 1.x wrote the token into the name as it was.
  • DeeZy refuses an output that is a source of the run or another job's output, even with --overwrite, and refuses --output with several inputs.
  • An interrupted or failed encode leaves no partial output.
  • --delay also takes frames at a frame rate, as in --delay=-3@23.976.

docs.title: Temp files and checks
docs.text:
• On Windows, FFmpeg's audio for dd, ddp, ddp-bluray, ac4 and aac goes straight into DEE through a pipe by default (--pipe auto). --pipe never writes the temp WAV, as 1.x did.
  • --reuse-temp-files doesn't reuse 1.x's Atmos and AC-4 temp folders.
  • DeeZy checks a job's options before it extracts or encodes anything, so a refused option fails at once.
  • With --config FILE, DeeZy no longer also reads the config it would find on its own.

docs.title: New in 2.0
docs.text:
• Formats: thd, thd-atmos, channel-based ac4, ac4-atmos and aac. See encode.
  • Atmos masters (DAMF and ADM BWF) as sources for the Atmos formats, and for dd and ddp, which DEE renders.
  • Commands: deezy measure, deezy bitrates and deezy tools.
  • Options: --dry-run, --print-commands, --keep-logs, --disable-lfe, --surround-3db, --pipe, --dee-shim and --no-shim, and for TrueHD Atmos --atmos-elements and --legacy-authoring.
  • dee_shim support: DD+ 7.1, the 7.1 Atmos modes, TrueHD --drc none, and faster DD+ Atmos and TrueHD encodes on AMD CPUs.
  • truehdd is needed only for a TrueHD Atmos source, not for every Atmos encode.

docs.title: Presets
docs.text:
Presets are simple command strings in the config under [presets].

Example

[presets]
streaming_ddp = "encode ddp --channels surround --bitrate 448"

Usage

deezy encode preset --name streaming_ddp input.mkv
deezy encode preset --name streaming_ddp --bitrate 640 input.mkv

Presets are validated and can be overridden by CLI flags.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
This page collects reference material: CLI options, batch JSON schema, and filename template tokens.

Batch summary JSON (top-level keys)

  • batch_info: timestamp, command, total_files, successful, failed, skipped, total_duration_seconds, max_parallel
  • results: array of per-file objects with input_file, output_file, status, start_time, end_time, duration_seconds, error

Output template tokens

  • {title}, {year}, {stem}, {stem-cleaned}, {source}, {lang}, {channels}, {worker}, {delay}, {opt-delay}

Every command's options are in the CLI reference, and deezy <command> --help prints them.

docs.title: Temp Management
docs.text:
DeeZy organizes temporary artifacts in a deterministic per-input job folder under the user's platform-specific application data directory by default (this uses platformdirs.user_data_dir() under the hood). For example:

  • Windows (typical): %APPDATA%\DeeZy\deezy\<job-folder>
  • Linux (typical): ~/.local/share/deezy/<job-folder>
  • macOS (typical): ~/Library/Application Support/deezy/<job-folder>

Each job gets its own short, deterministic folder (sanitized stem + short hash). If you prefer a centralized base, pass --temp-dir to place per-input sub-folders under your chosen location.

Commands

deezy temp info
deezy temp clean --max-age 24
deezy temp clean --dry-run

Options: --temp-dir, --reuse-temp-files, --keep-temp

Notes about reuse

  • Temporary artifacts are codec-scoped and tracked in a metadata file per job folder (naming convention: <output_stem>_metadata.json). The metadata stores encoder-scoped signatures and the basename of the produced file; reuse checks look for the produced basename inside the same job folder.
  • --reuse-temp-files implies --keep-temp so artifacts persist and can be reused by subsequent runs.

Path length and Windows UNC tips

  • On Windows, very long input/output paths or an explicit --temp-dir with a long base can trigger problems when downstream tools (DEE) open temporary files. If you see errors opening them (especially with UNC paths like \\?\UNC\...), try one of the following:
  • Use a shorter --temp-dir base located on the same machine as the encoder (e.g. a short local path) so per-job folders remain under the Windows path length limits.
  • Use --keep-temp so you can inspect the produced temp folder and paths.
  • Run deezy temp info to inspect where DeeZy places job folders on your system.

The code creates short job-folder names to reduce path length pressure, but if you still hit path-length limitations the explicit --temp-dir will be validated and may raise an error; prefer a short base when providing an explicit temporary directory.

docs.title: Output Filename Templates
docs.text:
Use --output-template to generate consistent output filenames when --output is not provided.

Example

deezy encode ddp --output-template "{title}_{year}_{stem}_{channels}_{delay}" input.mkv

Supported tokens: {title}, {year}, {stem}, {stem-cleaned}, {source}, {lang}, {channels}, {worker}, {delay}, {opt-delay}, {format}, {track}, {bitrate}, {bitrate-split}

opt-delay will return nothing if delay is equal to 0.

Use --output-preview to render a template without running the job.

{format} is the encode subcommand, such as ddp-atmos. {track} is the zero-based index from the selected audio or stream selector. {bitrate} is the resolved total in kbps and is empty for lossless formats. For a split of 1024:512, {bitrate} gives 1536 and {bitrate-split} gives 1024-512. The split token is empty for a single total.

docs.title: {stem} token
docs.text:
Automatically removes any type of DELAY Nms/s from the filename when used.

Example Input: Migration Some Random Stuff DELAY 1006ms.flac

Example Command: deezy encode dd --output-template "{stem} {opt-delay}"

Example Output: Migration Some Random Stuff.ac3

docs.title: {stem-cleaned} token
docs.text:
The {stem-cleaned} token is a cleaned version of the input file stem and is useful when you want a tidy, human-readable piece of the original filename without common metadata. The cleaner performs the following steps (in roughly this order):

  • Remove bracketed or parenthesized tags (e.g. [eng], (jpn)).
  • Strip explicit delay tokens such as DELAY 12ms or delay-5ms.
  • Remove numeric audio channel annotations such as 5.1, 2.0, 7.1ch, and 5ch.
  • Remove simple channel words commonly used as metadata: stereo, mono, dual mono.
  • Remove common codec and sample-rate tokens (e.g. ac3, eac3, flac, 48kHz, 96k) so they don't pollute titles.
  • Normalize separators (underscores, dots) into spaces and collapse repeated separators/whitespace.

Notes:

  • {stem} is ignored if {stem-cleaned} is used in the same template.
  • Leading numeric track numbers are preserved; this keeps filenames like 01 or 03 - Something meaningful when the numeric portion is the only useful label.

Examples (input stem -> {stem-cleaned}):

  • 01 - Main Title [eng] DELAY 12ms.eac3 -> 01 Main Title
  • Track_03 (eng) 48kHz 5.1.flac -> Track 03
  • 07 - Surround Mix [eng] 7.1ch.dts -> 07 Surround Mix
  • 03 - Multichannel [eng] 5ch.eac3 -> 03 Multichannel

docs.title: Tips & Best Practices
docs.text:
Short, practical guidance to get the most out of DeeZy.

  • Use presets for repeatable, shareable workflows. Put presets in your global config and reference them with deezy encode preset --name <name>.

  • When running batch jobs, set --max-parallel to a conservative value (1-4) and use --limit-ffmpeg / --limit-dee to avoid saturating systems.

  • Enable --batch-summary-output during testing to produce JSON results you can ingest into automation or QA pipelines.

  • To debug encoding failures, run with --dry-run to see the commands DeeZy would run, --keep-logs to keep what the tools print, or --keep-temp to inspect intermediate files, and re-run with --reuse-temp-files where possible.

  • For CI environments, use --output-preview to verify templates and paths without writing outputs.

  • When converting many files, consider running jobs on a dedicated machine with isolated --working-dir to keep logs and batch-results tidy.

  • Use deezy find and deezy info to validate inputs before running large batches.

  • Keep deezy-conf.toml under version control for reproducible results across machines.

  • If you rely on external executables (FFmpeg, DEE, truehdd, dee_shim), set full paths via --ffmpeg / --dee / --truehdd / --dee-shim in CI to avoid path resolution issues. deezy tools shows what DeeZy finds.

docs.title: Track Selection
docs.text:
DeeZy supports flexible track selection using FFmpeg-style notation.

Syntax

N — audio track N a:N — explicit audio track s:N — stream index N (any track type)

Examples

deezy encode ddp --track-index 0 input.mkv
deezy encode ddp --track-index a:1 input.mkv
deezy encode ddp --track-index s:2 input.mkv

Notes

  • Use s:N when matching FFmpeg stream numbering is important.
  • DeeZy validates s:N selects an audio stream and errors if not.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with deezy tools. It shows the FFmpeg, DEE tools (and their license), truehdd and dee_shim an encode would use, with each one's version and path, and exits with 1 when an encode couldn't run.

docs.title: Common messages
docs.text:
• "Failed to detect required dependencies: ...": DeeZy found no FFmpeg or DEE tools. Give the path with --ffmpeg or --dee, or under [dependencies] in the config. See Installation.
  • "truehdd is needed to decode a TrueHD Atmos source, and DeeZy didn't find it": give truehdd's path with --truehdd or under [dependencies]. Only a TrueHD Atmos source needs it.
  • "Configured dependency path does not exist: ...": a path given on the command line or in the config is wrong.
  • "DeeZy needs the DEE 6.7 command-line tools, but '...' reports ...": the DEE DeeZy found is another version, such as the single dee of DEE 5.2. Point --dee at the DEE 6.7 tools' folder, and see Migrating from 1.x.
  • "License file does not exist" or "Provided license file does not enable this tool": the DEE tools found no license that covers them. See DEE license.
  • "... needs dee_shim (0.3.0 or newer)": the encode needs dee_shim (DD+ 7.1, ddp-atmos --atmos-mode standard or bluray, TrueHD --drc none). Give its path with --dee-shim, or choose a layout or mode DEE encodes alone.
  • "Up-mixing is not supported.": the layout asked for has more channels than the source.
  • "Bitrate ... is invalid for this configuration. Using the next closest allowed bitrate: ...": deezy bitrates <format> lists the rates DEE takes.
  • "Output already exists: ...": the job is skipped. --overwrite replaces the file.
  • "The output would overwrite its own source" or "... is also the output of ... in this run": give each job its own name with --output, or an --output-template that tells them apart.
  • MediaInfo shows a 7.1 DD+ Atmos stream as plain Dolby Digital Plus: see ddp-atmos.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
deezy encode ddp --dry-run input.mkv
deezy encode ddp --keep-logs input.mkv
deezy --log-level debug encode ddp input.mkv
deezy --log-to-file encode ddp --keep-temp --temp-dir "C:\debug" input.mkv
  • --dry-run probes the source and prints the FFmpeg, truehdd and DEE commands without running them. --print-commands prints them as they start.
  • --keep-logs writes everything the tools print to <output>.log beside the output. If that location is unwritable, DeeZy saves the log in its local user log directory and prints the path.
  • --keep-temp keeps the job's temp files to look at.

If it still fails, open an issue with a short reproduction and the --keep-logs log.

docs.title: Windows long paths and UNC
docs.text:
If DEE or other tools fail to open temp files on Windows (especially with UNC paths like \\?\UNC\...), check for path-length problems and use a short temp base while debugging. Useful PowerShell checks:

# Check that the path exists (normalize \?\ prefix first if present)
$p = '\\?\UNC\SHARE\very\long\path\file.wav'
$norm = if ($p -like '\\?\*') { $p -replace '^\\\\\?\\', '' } else { $p }
Test-Path $norm

# Show total path length
$norm.Length

# If a path is too long, run with a short temp dir for debugging:
deezy --config deezy-conf.toml --log-to-file encode ddp --keep-temp --temp-dir 'C:\short_tmp' input.mkv

Prefer a short local --temp-dir base (for example C:\deezy_tmp) when processing files with long UNC or deep output paths. DeeZy already uses short job folders, but a short base makes Windows path-length limits less likely.

docs.title: Core commands
docs.text:
• deezy encode <format> — encode to dd, ddp, ddp-bluray, ddp-atmos, ac4, ac4-ims, ac4-atmos, aac, thd or thd-atmos (see encode)
  • deezy measure <file> — measure the loudness without encoding
  • deezy info <file> — show the audio tracks
  • deezy find <glob> — find files using glob patterns
  • deezy bitrates [format] — list the data rates and defaults
  • deezy tools — show the tools DeeZy finds
  • deezy config — manage configuration
  • deezy temp — temp folder management

docs.title: Global options
docs.text:
--config, --log-level, --log-to-file, --no-progress-bars, --version

Examples

# Encode to DDP (smart defaults)
deezy encode ddp input.mkv

# Use preset
deezy encode preset --name streaming_ddp input.mkv

# Batch encode
deezy --log-to-file encode ddp --max-parallel 4 *.mkv

# Inspect tracks
deezy info input.mkv

docs.title: Power management
docs.text: DeeZy prevents automatic system sleep and hibernation while an encode is in progress. The display can still turn off normally. Pass --allow-sleep, or set allow_sleep = true under [global_defaults], to disable this behavior.

docs.title: Track selection
docs.text:
Use --track-index with N, a:N or s:N (stream index) to pick which audio to encode. See Track Selection.

Temp management

deezy temp info
deezy temp clean --max-age 24

docs.title: Notes on temp directories
docs.text:
Deezy creates per-job temporary directories under the configured temp base. By default --keep-temp is false and each run uses a short unique per-run directory so concurrent runs of the same file/track won't collide and can be removed automatically. When --keep-temp is enabled, Deezy uses a stable per-track directory (useful for inspection or caching) but this directory may be shared between runs of the same track and is not automatically removed.

For TrueHD Atmos sources, --keep-temp retains the decoded master. Use --reuse-temp-files on a later encode with the same temp base to reuse it across output formats or filenames. The source file, track selector, warp mode, FFmpeg and truehdd must match. DeeZy checks all three DAMF components before reuse. Masters kept by older versions are decoded once to record this information.

docs.title: deezy bitrates
docs.text:

options:

docs.title: deezy encode aac
docs.text:
AAC through DEE, always 2.0. --aac-profile picks AAC-LC (the default, 192 kbps), HE-AAC (64) or HE-AAC v2 (56). DEE's AAC encoder can't only measure the loudness, so by default DeeZy leaves it as it is; --loudness-target corrects it. See also AAC.

usage: DeeZy encode aac [-h] [--ffmpeg FFMPEG] [--truehdd TRUEHDD] [--dee DEE]
                        [--track-index TRACK_INDEX] [--dee-shim DEE_SHIM]
                        [--no-shim] [--delay DELAY] [--keep-temp]
                        [--reuse-temp-files] [--temp-dir TEMP_DIR]
                        [--output OUTPUT] [--output-template OUTPUT_TEMPLATE]
                        [--output-preview] [--max-parallel MAX_PARALLEL]
                        [--jitter-ms JITTER_MS] [--allow-sleep] [--max-logs N]
                        [--max-batch-results N] [--working-dir WORKING_DIR]
                        [--batch-summary-output]
                        [--batch-output-dir BATCH_OUTPUT_DIR] [--overwrite]
                        [--keep-logs] [--print-commands] [--dry-run]
                        [--limit-ffmpeg LIMIT_FFMPEG] [--limit-dee LIMIT_DEE]
                        [--limit-truehdd LIMIT_TRUEHDD] [--bitrate BITRATE]
                        [--no-dialogue-intelligence]
                        [--loudness-preset {manual,atsc_a85,ebu_r128,freetv_op59,arib_b32}]
                        [--speech-threshold SPEECH_THRESHOLD]
                        [--loudness-target [-31..-8]]
                        [--peak-limit PEAK_LIMIT]
                        [--aac-profile {aaclc,heaac,heaacv2}]
                        [--pipe {auto,always,never}]
                        INPUT [INPUT ...]

positional arguments:
  INPUT
       Input file paths or directories

options:
  -h, --help
       show this help message and exit
  --ffmpeg, FFMPEG
       Path to FFmpeg.
  --truehdd, TRUEHDD
       Path to truehdd.
  --dee, DEE
       The folder of the DEE tools, or one of them.
  --track-index, TRACK_INDEX
       The source track. Supports: 'N' (audio track N), 'a:N' (audio track N), 's:N' (stream index N).
  --dee-shim, DEE_SHIM
       Path to dee_shim (0.3.0 or newer). DeeZy needs it for DD+ 7.1 and 7.0, ddp-atmos --atmos-mode standard and bluray, TrueHD --drc none, and to measure 7.1. It also runs every ddp-atmos, thd and thd-atmos encode through it, which is faster on AMD CPUs and keeps more of the source as it is (see --no-oamd-as-is and --no-as-is). Found beside the DEE tools, in apps/dee_shim or on PATH when not given.
  --no-shim
       Don't use dee_shim, even when it is found.
  --delay, DELAY
       The delay in milliseconds, seconds or frames at a frame rate, decimals allowed. Note '--delay=' is required! (--delay=-10.5ms / --delay=1.25s / --delay=-3@23.976; the rate may also be 24000/1001, ntsc, pal, film or ntsc-film).
  --keep-temp
       Keeps the temp files after finishing.
  --reuse-temp-files
       Attempt to reuse already-extracted temp files adjacent to the input file when the extractor command is identical. This implies --keep-temp.
  --temp-dir, TEMP_DIR
       Path to store temporary files to. If not specified this will automatically happen in the temp dir of the os.
  --output, OUTPUT
       The output file path. If not specified we will attempt to automatically add Delay/Language string to output file name.
  --output-template, OUTPUT_TEMPLATE
       Optional lightweight template to control auto-generated output filenames. Supported tokens: {title},{year},{stem},{stem-cleaned},{source},{lang},{channels},{worker},{delay},{opt-delay},{format},{track},{bitrate},{bitrate-split}.
  --output-preview
       When set, render and show template-based filenames but do not write outputs. Useful to validate templates before running batch jobs.
  --max-parallel, MAX_PARALLEL
       Maximum number of files to process in parallel (default: 1).
  --jitter-ms, JITTER_MS
       Maximum random jitter in milliseconds to apply before heavy phases (FFmpeg/DEE/truehdd). Helps avoid synchronization spikes when running parallel jobs. Default 0 (disabled).
  --allow-sleep
       Allow the system to sleep while encoding. By default, DeeZy prevents automatic system sleep without keeping the display on.
  --max-logs, N
       Maximum number of log files to keep in the working logs directory for this run. Overrides config value if provided. Use 0 to keep none.
  --max-batch-results, N
       Maximum number of batch-results JSON files to keep in the working batch-results directory for this run. Overrides config value if provided. Use 0 to keep none.
  --working-dir, WORKING_DIR
       Directory to use for DeeZy working files (logs and batch-results). Overrides config/default. If not set, uses the workspace beside the executable.
  --batch-summary-output
       Enable batch processing results summary (JSON format). Results will be saved to a 'batch-results' folder next to the executable by default.
  --batch-output-dir, BATCH_OUTPUT_DIR
       When used with --batch-summary-output, place all encoded outputs into this directory instead of writing them next to the input files.
  --overwrite
       Overwrite existing output files instead of failing.
  --keep-logs
       Writes the job's command lines and everything DEE, FFmpeg and truehdd print to '<output>.log' beside the output, when the job fails too. FFmpeg then runs at its info level.
  --print-commands
       Print each FFmpeg, truehdd and DEE command line as it starts.
  --dry-run
       Probe the input and print the FFmpeg, truehdd and DEE command lines the encode would run, without running them or writing any file.
  --limit-ffmpeg, LIMIT_FFMPEG
       Optional limit for concurrent FFmpeg processing. Defaults to --max-parallel if not set. If set higher than --max-parallel the value will be capped to --max-parallel and a warning will be emitted.
  --limit-dee, LIMIT_DEE
       Optional limit for concurrent DEE processing. Defaults to --max-parallel if not set. If set higher than --max-parallel the value will be capped to --max-parallel and a warning will be emitted.
  --limit-truehdd, LIMIT_TRUEHDD
       Optional limit for concurrent truehdd processing. Defaults to --max-parallel if not set. If set higher than --max-parallel the value will be capped to --max-parallel and a warning will be emitted.
  --bitrate, BITRATE
       The bitrate in Kbps (If too high or low for you desired layout, the bitrate will automatically be adjusted to the closest allowed bitrate).
  --no-dialogue-intelligence
       Dialogue intelligence disabled.
  --loudness-preset, {manual,atsc_a85,ebu_r128,freetv_op59,arib_b32}
       Measure to a loudness regulation (ATSC A/85, EBU R128, FreeTV OP59, ARIB B32) instead of the manual settings. Replaces --no-dialogue-intelligence and --speech-threshold.
  --speech-threshold, SPEECH_THRESHOLD
       [0-100] If the percentage of speech is higher than the threshold, the encoder uses speech gating to set the dialnorm value. (Otherwise, the encoder uses level gating).
  --loudness-target, [-31..-8]
       Measure and correct the loudness to this target (LKFS) instead of only measuring. Can't be combined with --custom-dialnorm.
  --peak-limit, PEAK_LIMIT
       Peak limit in dBTP used with --loudness-target (-12 to -0.1, must be at least 6 dB above the target). Defaults to the encoder's -2.
  --aac-profile, {aaclc,heaac,heaacv2}
       AAC profile: aaclc (56-576 kbps, default 192), heaac (16-143, default 64) or heaacv2 (14-63, default 56). The output is always 2.0.
  --pipe, {auto,always,never}
       How FFmpeg's audio reaches DEE. 'auto' (the default) pipes it straight into DEE on Windows and writes a temp WAV elsewhere or with --reuse-temp-files; 'always' pipes it or refuses the job; 'never' always writes the temp WAV.

usage: DeeZy encode ac4-ims [-h] [--ffmpeg FFMPEG] [--truehdd TRUEHDD]
                            [--dee DEE] [--track-index TRACK_INDEX]
                            [--dee-shim DEE_SHIM] [--no-shim] [--delay DELAY]
                            [--keep-temp] [--reuse-temp-files]
                            [--temp-dir TEMP_DIR] [--output OUTPUT]
                            [--output-template OUTPUT_TEMPLATE]

       Keeps DEE's own processing through dee_shim. By default dee_shim turns DEE's apodizing filter off at 96 kHz (thd), and codes an Atmos master of 16 elements or fewer as it is (thd-atmos), so the stream decodes sample for sample. Without dee_shim this changes nothing.
  --custom-dialnorm, CUSTOM_DIALNORM
       Custom dialnorm (0 disables custom dialnorm).
  --legacy-authoring
       Make the stream for older disc-authoring tools (DEE's legacy authoring). The stream then carries no warp mode.
  --atmos-elements, {12,14,16}
       The elements the stream codes the master's bed and objects into (DEE's number_of_elements). More keep more of the master's detail and make a bigger stream; Dolby's default is 12. Through dee_shim a master with no more elements than this decodes to it sample for sample. Default 16.
  --thd-warp-mode, {normal,warping,prologiciix,loro}
       The warp mode truehdd gives a TrueHD Atmos stream that has none. Without it the stream keeps none, which DEE renders as warping.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Encode a DAMF master:
deezy encode thd-atmos master.atmos
  • 12 elements, for older disc-authoring tools:
deezy encode thd-atmos --atmos-elements 12 --legacy-authoring master.wav

docs.title: deezy encode thd
docs.text:
Dolby TrueHD (lossless), 2.0, 5.1 or 7.1. When DeeZy finds dee_shim, the encode runs through it; at 96 kHz dee_shim then turns DEE's apodizing filter off, so the stream decodes sample for sample (--no-as-is keeps DEE's processing). --drc none needs dee_shim. See also TrueHD.

usage: DeeZy encode thd [-h] [--ffmpeg FFMPEG] [--truehdd TRUEHDD] [--dee DEE]
                        [--track-index TRACK_INDEX] [--dee-shim DEE_SHIM]
                        [--no-shim] [--delay DELAY] [--keep-temp]
                        [--reuse-temp-files] [--temp-dir TEMP_DIR]
                        [--output OUTPUT] [--output-template OUTPUT_TEMPLATE]
                        [--output-preview] [--max-parallel MAX_PARALLEL]
                        [--jitter-ms JITTER_MS] [--allow-sleep] [--max-logs N]
                        [--max-batch-results N] [--working-dir WORKING_DIR]
                        [--batch-summary-output]
                        [--batch-output-dir BATCH_OUTPUT_DIR] [--overwrite]
                        [--keep-logs] [--print-commands] [--dry-run]
                        [--limit-ffmpeg LIMIT_FFMPEG] [--limit-dee LIMIT_DEE]
                        [--limit-truehdd LIMIT_TRUEHDD]
                        [--no-dialogue-intelligence]
                        [--loudness-preset {manual,atsc_a85,ebu_r128,freetv_op59,arib_b32}]
                        [--speech-threshold SPEECH_THRESHOLD]
                        [--channels {0,2,6,8}] [--layout {5.1.2}]
                        [--disable-lfe] [--surround-3db]
                        [--drc {film_standard,film_light,music_standard,music_light,speech,none}]
                        [--no-as-is] [--custom-dialnorm CUSTOM_DIALNORM]
                        INPUT [INPUT ...]

positional arguments:
  INPUT
       Input file paths or directories

options:
  -h, --help
       show this help message and exit
  --ffmpeg, FFMPEG
       Path to FFmpeg.
  --truehdd, TRUEHDD
       Path to truehdd.
  --dee, DEE
       The folder of the DEE tools, or one of them.
  --track-index, TRACK_INDEX
       The source track. Supports: 'N' (audio track N), 'a:N' (audio track N), 's:N' (stream index N).
  --dee-shim, DEE_SHIM
       Path to dee_shim (0.3.0 or newer). DeeZy needs it for DD+ 7.1 and 7.0, ddp-atmos --atmos-mode standard and bluray, TrueHD --drc none, and to measure 7.1. It also runs every ddp-atmos, thd and thd-atmos encode through it, which is faster on AMD CPUs and keeps more of the source as it is (see --no-oamd-as-is and --no-as-is). Found beside the DEE tools, in apps/dee_shim or on PATH when not given.
  --no-shim
       Don't use dee_shim, even when it is found.
  --delay, DELAY
       The delay in milliseconds, seconds or frames at a frame rate, decimals allowed. Note '--delay=' is required! (--delay=-10.5ms / --delay=1.25s / --delay=-3@23.976; the rate may also be 24000/1001, ntsc, pal, film or ntsc-film).
  --keep-temp
       Keeps the temp files after finishing.
  --reuse-temp-files
       Attempt to reuse already-extracted temp files adjacent to the input file when the extractor command is identical. This implies --keep-temp.
  --temp-dir, TEMP_DIR
       Path to store temporary files to. If not specified this will automatically happen in the temp dir of the os.
  --output, OUTPUT
       The output file path. If not specified we will attempt to automatically add Delay/Language string to output file name.
  --output-template, OUTPUT_TEMPLATE
       Optional lightweight template to control auto-generated output filenames. Supported tokens: {title},{year},{stem},{stem-cleaned},{source},{lang},{channels},{worker},{delay},{opt-delay},{format},{track},{bitrate},{bitrate-split}.
  --output-preview
       When set, render and show template-based filenames but do not write outputs. Useful to validate templates before running batch jobs.
  --max-parallel, MAX_PARALLEL
       Maximum number of files to process in parallel (default: 1).
  --jitter-ms, JITTER_MS
       Maximum random jitter in milliseconds to apply before heavy phases (FFmpeg/DEE/truehdd). Helps avoid synchronization spikes when running parallel jobs. Default 0 (disabled).
  --allow-sleep
       Allow the system to sleep while encoding. By default, DeeZy prevents automatic system sleep without keeping the display on.
  --max-logs, N
       Maximum number of log files to keep in the working logs directory for this run. Overrides config value if provided. Use 0 to keep none.
  --max-batch-results, N
       Maximum number of batch-results JSON files to keep in the working batch-results directory for this run. Overrides config value if provided. Use 0 to keep none.
  --working-dir, WORKING_DIR
       Directory to use for DeeZy working files (logs and batch-results). Overrides config/default. If not set, uses the workspace beside the executable.
  --batch-summary-output
       Enable batch processing results summary (JSON format). Results will be saved to a 'batch-results' folder next to the executable by default.
  --batch-output-dir, BATCH_OUTPUT_DIR
       When used with --batch-summary-output, place all encoded outputs into this directory instead of writing them next to the input files.
  --overwrite
       Overwrite existing output files instead of failing.
  --keep-logs
       Writes the job's command lines and everything DEE, FFmpeg and truehdd print to '<output>.log' beside the output, when the job fails too. FFmpeg then runs at its info level.
  --print-commands
       Print each FFmpeg, truehdd and DEE command line as it starts.
  --dry-run
       Probe the input and print the FFmpeg, truehdd and DEE command lines the encode would run, without running them or writing any file.
  --limit-ffmpeg, LIMIT_FFMPEG
       Optional limit for concurrent FFmpeg processing. Defaults to --max-parallel if not set. If set higher than --max-parallel the value will be capped to --max-parallel and a warning will be emitted.
  --limit-dee, LIMIT_DEE
       Optional limit for concurrent DEE processing. Defaults to --max-parallel if not set. If set higher than --max-parallel the value will be capped to --max-parallel and a warning will be emitted.
  --limit-truehdd, LIMIT_TRUEHDD
       Optional limit for concurrent truehdd processing. Defaults to --max-parallel if not set. If set higher than --max-parallel the value will be capped to --max-parallel and a warning will be emitted.
  --no-dialogue-intelligence
       Dialogue intelligence disabled.
  --loudness-preset, {manual,atsc_a85,ebu_r128,freetv_op59,arib_b32}
       Measure to a loudness regulation (ATSC A/85, EBU R128, FreeTV OP59, ARIB B32) instead of the manual settings. Replaces --no-dialogue-intelligence and --speech-threshold.
  --speech-threshold, SPEECH_THRESHOLD
       [0-100] If the percentage of speech is higher than the threshold, the encoder uses speech gating to set the dialnorm value. (Otherwise, the encoder uses level gating).
  --channels, {0,2,6,8}
       The number of channels: 2.0, 5.1 or 7.1. Auto takes the smallest that holds every source channel, filling the rest with silence.
  --layout, {5.1.2}
       Preserve a 5.1.2 source with side surrounds and front heights (requires dee_shim). Use with automatic or 8 channels.
  --disable-lfe
       Silence the LFE channel while keeping it in the TrueHD layout.
  --surround-3db
       Lowers the surround channels by 3 dB (DEE's surround_3dB_attenuation). Off by default, as in DEE.
  --drc, {film_standard,film_light,music_standard,music_light,speech,none}
       Dynamic range compression profile, for every presentation. none (only the peak protection) needs dee_shim.
  --no-as-is
       Keeps DEE's own processing through dee_shim. By default dee_shim turns DEE's apodizing filter off at 96 kHz (thd), and codes an Atmos master of 16 elements or fewer as it is (thd-atmos), so the stream decodes sample for sample. Without dee_shim this changes nothing.
  --custom-dialnorm, CUSTOM_DIALNORM
       Custom dialnorm (0 disables custom dialnorm).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Encode with automatic channel selection:
deezy encode thd movie.mkv
  • Preserve 5.1.2 with side surrounds and front heights (needs dee_shim):
deezy encode thd --layout 5.1.2 input.wav
  • 7.1 with no dynamic range compression (needs dee_shim):
deezy encode thd --channels 8 --drc none movie.mkv

docs.title: deezy encode
docs.text:
deezy encode <format> encodes each input to one format. Each format's page lists its options.

Format Output Page dd Dolby Digital (AC-3), .ac3 encode dd ddp Dolby Digital Plus (E-AC-3), .ec3 encode ddp ddp-bluray Dolby Digital Plus 7.1 for Blu-ray, .ec3 encode ddp-bluray ddp-atmos Dolby Digital Plus with Dolby Atmos, .ec3 encode ddp-atmos ac4 Channel-based Dolby AC-4, .ac4 encode ac4 ac4-ims Dolby AC-4 immersive stereo, .ac4 encode ac4-ims ac4-atmos Dolby AC-4 with Dolby Atmos, .ac4 encode ac4-atmos aac AAC-LC, HE-AAC or HE-AAC v2, .aac encode aac thd Dolby TrueHD, .thd encode thd thd-atmos Dolby TrueHD with Dolby Atmos, .thd encode thd-atmos preset The format the preset names encode preset 
usage: DeeZy encode [-h] AUDIO_FORMAT ...

positional arguments:
  AUDIO_FORMAT
    dd          Dolby Digital (AC-3)
    ddp         Dolby Digital Plus (E-AC-3)
    ddp-bluray  Dolby Digital Plus for Blu-ray
    ddp-atmos   Dolby Digital Plus with Dolby Atmos (JOC)
    ac4         Channel-based Dolby AC-4
    ac4-ims     Dolby AC-4 immersive stereo (IMS)
    ac4-atmos   Dolby AC-4 with Dolby Atmos
    aac         AAC (AAC-LC, HE-AAC, HE-AAC v2)
    thd         Dolby TrueHD
    thd-atmos   Dolby TrueHD with Dolby Atmos
    preset      Encode using a preset configuration (format determined from
                preset).

options:
  -h, --help    show this help message and exit

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Encode one file. The output goes beside it, named from the source:
deezy encode dd movie.mkv
  • Encode a folder's files two at a time and keep the temp files:
deezy encode ddp --max-parallel 2 --keep-temp "media/*.mkv"
  • Show the names an output template gives, without encoding:
deezy encode dd --output-template "{title} [{lang}]" --output-preview "media/*.mkv"
  • Print the commands an encode would run, without running them:
deezy encode ddp --dry-run movie.mkv

docs.title: deezy measure
docs.text:
Measures each input's loudness with DEE, without encoding. --output or --output-dir saves DEE's loudness manifest (JSON).

DEE measures 1.0, 2.0 and 5.1, and Atmos as its binaural and 5.1 renders. A source of 3 to 5 channels is measured as 5.1 with silent channels added, and one of 7 or 8 channels as 7.1 through dee_shim. Neither changes the loudness. DeeZy refuses a source of more channels, since a downmix would.

usage: DeeZy measure [-h] [--ffmpeg FFMPEG] [--truehdd TRUEHDD] [--dee DEE]
                     [--track-index TRACK_INDEX] [--dee-shim DEE_SHIM]
                     [--no-shim] [--output OUTPUT | --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR]
                     [--temp-dir TEMP_DIR] [--keep-temp] [--overwrite]
                     [--print-commands] [--dry-run]
                     [--no-dialogue-intelligence]
                     [--loudness-preset {manual,atsc_a85,ebu_r128,freetv_op59,arib_b32}]
                     [--speech-threshold SPEECH_THRESHOLD]
                     [--pipe {auto,always,never}]
                     [--thd-warp-mode {normal,warping,prologiciix,loro}]
                     INPUT [INPUT ...]

positional arguments:
  INPUT
       Input file paths or directories

options:
  -h, --help
       show this help message and exit
  --ffmpeg, FFMPEG
       Path to FFmpeg.
  --truehdd, TRUEHDD
       Path to truehdd.
  --dee, DEE
       The folder of the DEE tools, or one of them.
  --track-index, TRACK_INDEX
       The source track. Supports: 'N' (audio track N), 'a:N' (audio track N), 's:N' (stream index N).
  --dee-shim, DEE_SHIM
       Path to dee_shim (0.3.0 or newer). DeeZy needs it for DD+ 7.1 and 7.0, ddp-atmos --atmos-mode standard and bluray, TrueHD --drc none, and to measure 7.1. It also runs every ddp-atmos, thd and thd-atmos encode through it, which is faster on AMD CPUs and keeps more of the source as it is (see --no-oamd-as-is and --no-as-is). Found beside the DEE tools, in apps/dee_shim or on PATH when not given.
  --no-shim
       Don't use dee_shim, even when it is found.
  --output, OUTPUT
       Save DEE's loudness manifest (JSON) to this file. One input only.
  --output-dir, OUTPUT_DIR
       Save each input's loudness manifest (JSON) in this directory, as <input name>.loudness.json.
  --temp-dir, TEMP_DIR
       Path to store temporary files to. If not specified this will automatically happen in the temp dir of the os.
  --keep-temp
       Keeps the temp files after finishing.
  --overwrite
       Overwrite an existing saved manifest instead of failing.
  --print-commands
       Print each FFmpeg, truehdd and DEE command line as it starts.
  --dry-run
       Probe the input and print the FFmpeg, truehdd and DEE command lines the measurement would run, without running them or writing any file.
  --no-dialogue-intelligence
       Dialogue intelligence disabled.
  --loudness-preset, {manual,atsc_a85,ebu_r128,freetv_op59,arib_b32}
       Measure to a loudness regulation (ATSC A/85, EBU R128, FreeTV OP59, ARIB B32) instead of the manual settings. Replaces --no-dialogue-intelligence and --speech-threshold.
  --speech-threshold, SPEECH_THRESHOLD
       [0-100] If the percentage of speech is higher than the threshold, the encoder uses speech gating to set the dialnorm value. (Otherwise, the encoder uses level gating).
  --pipe, {auto,always,never}
       How FFmpeg's audio reaches DEE. 'auto' (the default) pipes it straight into DEE on Windows and writes a temp WAV elsewhere or with --reuse-temp-files; 'always' pipes it or refuses the job; 'never' always writes the temp WAV.
  --thd-warp-mode, {normal,warping,prologiciix,loro}
       The warp mode truehdd gives a TrueHD Atmos stream that has none. Without it the stream keeps none, which DEE renders as warping.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Measure one file:
deezy measure movie.mkv
  • Measure to EBU R128 and save the manifest:
deezy measure --loudness-preset ebu_r128 --output movie.loudness.json movie.mkv
  • Save each file's manifest in a folder:
deezy measure --output-dir loudness "media/*.mkv"

docs.title: deezy tools
docs.text:
Shows the FFmpeg, truehdd, DEE tools (and their license) and dee_shim an encode would use, with each one's version and path.

usage: DeeZy tools [-h] [--ffmpeg FFMPEG] [--truehdd TRUEHDD] [--dee DEE]
                   [--dee-shim DEE_SHIM] [--no-shim]

Lists FFmpeg, truehdd, the DEE tools (and their license) and dee_shim as an
encode finds them: the paths given here or in the config's [dependencies],
else beside DeeZy (apps/...), else on PATH. Exits with 1 when an encode
couldn't run: no FFmpeg, no DEE 6.7, or a path given that doesn't work.

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --ffmpeg FFMPEG      Path to FFmpeg.
  --truehdd TRUEHDD    Path to truehdd.
  --dee DEE            The folder of the DEE tools, or one of them.
  --dee-shim DEE_SHIM  Path to dee_shim.
  --no-shim            Report dee_shim as turned off.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• The tools DeeZy finds:
deezy tools
  • Check a DEE folder:
deezy tools --dee "apps/dee-6.7.0"

docs.title: deezy
docs.text:
Global options go before the command, as in deezy --log-level debug encode ddp movie.mkv. Each command has its own page.

usage: DeeZy [-h] [--version] [--config CONFIG_FILE]
             [--log-level {critical,error,warning,info,debug}] [--log-to-file]
             [--no-progress-bars]
             {encode,find,info,measure,config,bitrates,tools,temp} ...

positional arguments:
  {encode,find,info,measure,config,bitrates,tools,temp}
    encode              Encode management
    find                Find management
    info                Info management
    measure             Measure loudness with DEE (1.0, 2.0, 5.1, 7.1 through
                        dee_shim, and Atmos; 3 to 5 channels as 5.1, 7 as 7.1)
    config              Configuration management
    bitrates            List the data rates each format and mode takes, and
                        the defaults
    tools               List the tools DeeZy finds, where they are and their
                        versions
    temp                Temporary folder management

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit
  --config CONFIG_FILE  Path to configuration file (default: deezy-conf.toml
                        beside executable)
  --log-level {critical,error,warning,info,debug}
                        Sets the log level (defaults to INFO).
  --log-to-file         Write log to file (defaults to input path with suffix
                        of .log).
  --no-progress-bars    Disables progress bars on level INFO (disabled for
                        DEBUG or higher).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Encode a file to Dolby Digital Plus:
deezy encode ddp movie.mkv
  • Use a config file other than the one DeeZy finds:
deezy --config my-conf.toml encode dd --bitrate 448 movie.mkv
  • Log everything, without progress bars:
deezy --log-level debug --no-progress-bars encode ddp-atmos movie.mkv
  • List the tools DeeZy finds:
deezy tools

docs.title: AAC (aac)
docs.text:
AAC through DEE's AAC encoder, written as .aac. The output is always 2.0. Every option is on deezy encode aac.

deezy encode aac movie.mkv
deezy encode aac --aac-profile heaac --bitrate 48 movie.mkv

--aac-profile picks AAC-LC (aaclc, the default), HE-AAC (heaac) or HE-AAC v2 (heaacv2).

docs.title: Data rates
docs.text:
aac --aac-profile aaclc (default)
  2.0   default 192: 56-576
aac --aac-profile heaac
  2.0   default 64: 16-143
aac --aac-profile heaacv2
  2.0   default 56: 14-63

DEE's AAC delay depends on the rate; DeeZy compensates it for each one.

docs.title: Loudness
docs.text:
AAC carries no loudness metadata, and DEE's AAC encoder can't only measure, so by default DeeZy leaves the loudness as it is.

  • --loudness-target (with --peak-limit) corrects the audio to that loudness, as for Dolby Digital.
  • --loudness-preset corrects it to that regulation. It can't be combined with --loudness-target.

docs.title: Dolby AC-4 with Dolby Atmos (ac4-atmos)
docs.text:
Dolby AC-4 with Dolby Atmos, written as .ac4. DeeZy uses DEE's level 3, for film and TV. Every option is on deezy encode ac4-atmos.

deezy encode ac4-atmos movie.mkv
deezy encode ac4-atmos --bitrate 768 master.wav

docs.title: Sources
docs.text: The source is a TrueHD Atmos track (truehdd decodes it to a DAMF master first, so DeeZy needs truehdd), a DAMF master (the .atmos file, beside its .atmos.metadata and .atmos.audio) or an ADM BWF master (.wav).

docs.title: Data rates
docs.text:
ac4-atmos
  atmos default 448: 256, 320, 448, 768

DeeZy's default is a step above DEE's own, 320 kbps.

docs.title: Loudness and DRC
docs.text: DEE only measures the loudness and writes it into the stream; --loudness-preset works as for Dolby Digital. The four device DRC profiles are --flat-panel-drc, --home-theatre-drc, --portable-headphones-drc and --portable-speakers-drc.

docs.title: Warp mode
docs.text: A TrueHD Atmos stream that carries no warp mode reaches DEE with none, which DEE renders as warping, its own default. --thd-warp-mode gives such a stream one (normal, warping, prologiciix or loro). A stream that has a warp mode keeps it. DeeZy 1.x gave every such stream normal.

docs.title: Sync
docs.text: DeeZy compensates the delay DEE's manifest reports. It hasn't been checked against an AC-4 decoder.

docs.title: Dolby AC-4 immersive stereo (ac4-ims)
docs.text:
Dolby AC-4 immersive stereo (IMS): a 2.0 AC-4 stream made from an immersive or surround mix, written as .ac4. Every option is on deezy encode ac4-ims. DeeZy 1.x called this format ac4.

deezy encode ac4-ims movie.mkv
deezy encode ac4-ims --encoding-profile ims_music --bitrate 320 concert.mkv

docs.title: Sources
docs.text: TrueHD Atmos, an Atmos master (DAMF or ADM BWF) or a channel-based source of 6 channels or more (7.1 is downmixed to 5.1 first, which is what DEE takes).

docs.title: Data rates
docs.text:
ac4-ims
  2.0   default 256: 64, 96, 128, 144, 256, 320

A rate DEE doesn't take becomes the closest one it does, with a warning.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text: --encoding-profile is ims (the default) or ims_music, for music. With ims_music DeeZy sets the four device DRC profiles to music_light and turns dialogue intelligence off, as DEE requires.

docs.title: Loudness and DRC
docs.text: DEE measures the loudness and writes it into the stream; --loudness-preset works as for Dolby Digital. --ddp-drc and the four device profiles (--flat-panel-drc, --home-theatre-drc, --portable-headphones-drc, --portable-speakers-drc) pick the DRC.

docs.title: Warp mode
docs.text: A TrueHD Atmos stream that carries no warp mode reaches DEE with none, which DEE renders as warping, its own default. --thd-warp-mode gives such a stream one (normal, warping, prologiciix or loro). A stream that has a warp mode keeps it. DeeZy 1.x gave every such stream normal.

docs.title: Sync
docs.text: DeeZy keeps 1.x's 256-sample delay compensation for IMS. It hasn't been measured against an AC-4 decoder.

docs.title: Dolby AC-4 (ac4)
docs.text:
Channel-based Dolby AC-4, written as .ac4. Every option is on deezy encode ac4.

In DeeZy 1.x ac4 made immersive stereo, which is now ac4-ims. DeeZy logs a notice each time ac4 runs.

deezy encode ac4 movie.mkv
deezy encode ac4 --channels 2 --bitrate 128 movie.mkv

docs.title: Layouts
docs.text: --channels picks 2.0 (2) or 5.1 (6). Auto (0, the default) gives a source of 5 channels or more 5.1 (a 5.0 source gets a silent LFE; DEE downmixes 7.1) and a smaller one 2.0. A mono source becomes 2.0 at -3 dB per channel, so it measures as loud as the mono. --disable-lfe gives 5.1 a silent LFE.

docs.title: Loudness
docs.text: DEE measures the loudness and writes it into the stream. --loudness-target (-31 to -10 LKFS for AC-4) and --peak-limit correct it, and --loudness-preset measures to a regulation, as for Dolby Digital.

docs.title: DRC
docs.text: AC-4 has a DRC profile per kind of device: --flat-panel-drc, --home-theatre-drc, --portable-headphones-drc and --portable-speakers-drc. They take every profile but none.

docs.title: Sync
docs.text: DeeZy compensates the delay DEE's manifest reports. It hasn't been checked against an AC-4 decoder.

docs.title: Dolby Digital (dd)
docs.text:
Dolby Digital (AC-3), written as .ac3, for players that don't decode Dolby Digital Plus. Every option is on deezy encode dd.

deezy encode dd movie.mkv
deezy encode dd --channels 2 --bitrate 192 movie.mkv

docs.title: Layouts
docs.text:
--channels picks 1.0 (1), 2.0 (2) or 5.1 (6). With 0 (auto, the default) DeeZy follows the source: 1 channel gives 1.0, 2 to 5 give 2.0 (a 5.0 source gives 5.0) and 6 or more give 5.1.

  • A source with no LFE (5.0, 7.0) is coded as 5.0. --upmix-50-to-51 codes a 5.0 source as 5.1 with a silent LFE instead.
  • --disable-lfe codes 5.1 as 5.0.
  • --stereo-down-mix picks how a stereo output is mixed from more channels: loro (the default), ltrt or dpl2. With dpl2, a 2.0 output gets FFmpeg's Dolby Pro Logic II mix; any other layout is marked ltrt, because DEE's Dolby Digital encoder takes no Pro Logic II downmix mode.
  • --lo-ro-center, --lo-ro-surround, --lt-rt-center and --lt-rt-surround set the levels a player uses when it downmixes the stream (-3 dB by default).

docs.title: Data rates
docs.text:
dd
  1.0   default 192: 96, 112, 128, 160, 192, 224, 256, 320, 384, 448, 512, 576, 640
  2.0   default 224: 96, 112, 128, 160, 192, 224, 256, 320, 384, 448, 512, 576, 640
  5.1   default 448: 224, 256, 320, 384, 448, 512, 576, 640

--bitrate picks a rate; one DEE doesn't take becomes the closest one it does, with a warning. The config's [default_bitrates] changes the defaults (see Configuration).

docs.title: Loudness
docs.text:
By default DEE measures the loudness (ITU-R BS.1770-4) and writes the measured dialnorm into the stream. The audio isn't changed.

  • --custom-dialnorm -27 writes that dialnorm without measuring.
  • --loudness-target -24 measures and corrects the audio to that loudness (-31 to -8 LKFS). --peak-limit (-12 to -0.1 dBTP, at least 6 dB above the target) sets the true-peak limit, -2 by default. Neither works with --custom-dialnorm.
  • --loudness-preset (atsc_a85, ebu_r128, freetv_op59 or arib_b32) measures to that regulation instead of the manual settings, so --no-dialogue-intelligence and --speech-threshold don't apply and it can't be combined with --loudness-target. --custom-dialnorm still wins. A preset changes the measured dialnorm: on one Atmos clip manual gave -18 and ebu_r128 gave -13.
deezy encode dd --loudness-target -24 movie.mkv
deezy encode dd --loudness-preset ebu_r128 movie.mkv

docs.title: Processing
docs.text:
• --drc-line-mode and --drc-rf-mode pick the dynamic range compression profiles (film_light by default; none turns it off). See DRC.
  • --surround-3db lowers the surround channels by 3 dB. It is off by default, as in DEE (DeeZy 1.x turned it on).
  • --no-surround-90-deg-phase-shift turns off the surround phase shift.
  • --no-low-pass-filter turns off the LFE's low-pass filter.

docs.title: From an Atmos source
docs.text: A TrueHD Atmos track is encoded from FFmpeg's 7.1 decode of it. DEE renders an Atmos master (DAMF or ADM BWF) to the layout itself, 5.1 at most.

docs.title: Dolby Digital Plus with Dolby Atmos (ddp-atmos)
docs.text:
Dolby Digital Plus with Dolby Atmos (JOC), written as .ec3. Every option is on deezy encode ddp-atmos. DeeZy 1.x called this format atmos.

deezy encode ddp-atmos movie.mkv
deezy encode ddp-atmos --atmos-mode bluray master.atmos

docs.title: Sources
docs.text: The source is a TrueHD Atmos track (truehdd decodes it to a DAMF master first, so DeeZy needs truehdd), a DAMF master (the .atmos file, beside its .atmos.metadata and .atmos.audio) or an ADM BWF master (.wav). A channel-based source is refused.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
--atmos-mode Backbone Default rate Needs dee_shim streaming (default) 5.1 448 kbps no standard 7.1 as E-AC-3 1152 kbps yes bluray 7.1 with an AC-3 core 1280 kbps yes

Without dee_shim, DEE's own Blu-ray mode makes a 5.1.2 backbone, so DeeZy refuses standard and bluray.

docs.title: Data rates
docs.text:
ddp-atmos --atmos-mode streaming (default)
  atmos default 448: 384, 448, 576, 640, 768, 1024
ddp-atmos --atmos-mode bluray
  atmos default 1280, needs dee_shim: 1152, 1280, 1408, 1512, 1536, 1664
        R0:R1 (dee_shim): AC-3 core 224, 256, 320, 384, 448, 512, 576, 640, dependent 32-1024 kbps
ddp-atmos --atmos-mode standard
  atmos default 1152, needs dee_shim: 448-2048
        R0:R1 (dee_shim): E-AC-3 core 32-1024, dependent 32-1024 kbps

DEE fails some standard streams below about 432 kbps, depending on the content, so DeeZy starts at 448 kbps when you request a single total. With an explicit split, the encoder also needs enough room in the dependent substream for the master's JOC metadata.

docs.title: Through dee_shim
docs.text:
When DeeZy finds dee_shim, every ddp-atmos encode runs through it:

  • dee_shim codes the master's object metadata as it is (--oamd-as-is on). --no-oamd-as-is lets DEE smooth it, as plain DEE does, and gives plain DEE's output.
  • --no-surround-90-deg-phase-shift turns off the backbone's surround phase shift. It needs dee_shim.

docs.title: Loudness
docs.text: From a master DEE can only measure the loudness (the default) or write a set dialnorm (--custom-dialnorm); it can't correct it. --loudness-preset works as for Dolby Digital.

docs.title: Warp mode
docs.text: A TrueHD Atmos stream that carries no warp mode reaches DEE with none, which DEE renders as warping, its own default. --thd-warp-mode gives such a stream one (normal, warping, prologiciix or loro). A stream that has a warp mode keeps it. DeeZy 1.x gave every such stream normal.

docs.title: MediaInfo
docs.text: MediaInfo can show a 7.1 (standard or bluray) stream from DEE as plain "Dolby Digital Plus", without Atmos. DEE splits the Atmos metadata across the stream in a way MediaInfo misreads; plain DEE's output shows the same, and the stream is fine.

docs.title: Dolby Digital Plus for Blu-ray (ddp-bluray)
docs.text:
Dolby Digital Plus 7.1 as Blu-ray carries it: an AC-3 core with an E-AC-3 extension, written as .ec3. Every option is on deezy encode ddp-bluray. For Blu-ray secondary audio use ddp --bluray-secondary.

deezy encode ddp-bluray movie.mkv
deezy encode ddp-bluray --bitrate 1664 movie.mkv

docs.title: Layouts
docs.text: The output is 7.1. A 7.0 source is coded as 7.0 through dee_shim, else as 7.1 with a silent LFE; --disable-lfe does the same. A source of fewer channels is refused (DeeZy doesn't up-mix), and so is an Atmos master: DEE's Blu-ray mode doesn't take one. Use ddp or ddp-atmos for those.

docs.title: Data rates
docs.text:
ddp-bluray
  7.1   default 1280: 768, 1024, 1280, 1536, 1664
        R0:R1 (dee_shim): AC-3 core 224, 256, 320, 384, 448, 512, 576, 640, dependent 32-1024 kbps
ddp --bluray-secondary (Blu-ray secondary audio)
  2.0   default 192: 96, 128, 160, 192, 224, 256
  5.1   default 192: 160, 192, 224, 256

docs.title: Loudness
docs.text: DEE measures the loudness and writes the measured dialnorm. --custom-dialnorm and --loudness-preset work as for Dolby Digital; --loudness-target isn't available for Blu-ray.

docs.title: Processing
docs.text: DRC, --surround-3db (off by default), the phase shift, the LFE low-pass filter and the downmix options work as for Dolby Digital.

docs.title: Dolby Digital Plus (ddp)
docs.text:
Dolby Digital Plus (E-AC-3), written as .ec3. Every option is on deezy encode ddp.

deezy encode ddp movie.mkv
deezy encode ddp --channels 8 --bitrate 1024 movie.mkv

docs.title: Layouts
docs.text:
--channels picks 1.0 (1), 2.0 (2), 5.1 (6) or 7.1 (8). Auto (0, the default) follows the source as for Dolby Digital, and gives an 8-channel source 7.1 when DeeZy has dee_shim, else 5.1 with a notice.

  • 7.1 and 7.0 need dee_shim: DEE alone codes DD+ 7.1 only for Blu-ray (see ddp-bluray). Without dee_shim, --channels 8 is refused.
  • A source with no LFE is coded as 5.0, or a 7.0 source as 7.0 through dee_shim (5.0 without it). --upmix-50-to-51 codes a 5.0 source as 5.1 with a silent LFE.
  • --disable-lfe codes 5.1 as 5.0 and 7.1 as 7.0 (through dee_shim).
  • --stereo-down-mix (loro by default, ltrt or dpl2) picks how DEE mixes a 2.0 output, and the downmix it marks in the stream for players. DD+ takes dpl2 for every layout. The downmix levels work as for DD.

docs.title: Blu-ray secondary audio
docs.text:
--bluray-secondary makes Blu-ray secondary audio: 2.0 or 5.1, at the rates listed on ddp-bluray (192 kbps by default). A rate it doesn't take becomes the closest one it does, with a warning. --loudness-target works with it; --user-data doesn't. DEE keeps the LFE of secondary audio, so --disable-lfe gives it a silent one.

deezy encode ddp --bluray-secondary --channels 2 movie.mkv

docs.title: Loudness
docs.text: As for Dolby Digital: DEE measures the loudness and writes the measured dialnorm, and --custom-dialnorm, --loudness-target and --loudness-preset work the same way.

docs.title: Other options
docs.text:
• --user-data N writes a user data ID into the stream (-1, the default, writes none).
  • DRC, --surround-3db (off by default), the phase shift and the LFE low-pass filter work as for Dolby Digital.

docs.title: From an Atmos source
docs.text: As for Dolby Digital: a TrueHD Atmos track is encoded from FFmpeg's 7.1 decode, and DEE renders an Atmos master to 5.1 at most. Use ddp-atmos to keep the objects.

docs.title: Dolby TrueHD with Dolby Atmos (thd-atmos)
docs.text:
Dolby TrueHD with Dolby Atmos, written as .thd. Every option is on deezy encode thd-atmos.

deezy encode thd-atmos master.atmos
deezy encode thd-atmos --atmos-elements 12 movie.mkv

docs.title: Sources
docs.text: The source is a TrueHD Atmos track (truehdd decodes it to a DAMF master first, so DeeZy needs truehdd), a DAMF master (the .atmos file, beside its .atmos.metadata and .atmos.audio) or an ADM BWF master (.wav). Besides the Atmos presentation, DEE writes 7.1, 5.1 and 2.0 presentations it downmixes from it.

docs.title: Elements
docs.text: --atmos-elements (12, 14 or 16, default 16) sets how many elements the stream codes the master's bed and objects into. More keep more of the master's detail and make a bigger stream; Dolby's default is 12. A master with more elements than that is clustered into them, and DeeZy logs why. MediaInfo's bed and object counts follow the stream's element count.

docs.title: Legacy authoring
docs.text: Off by default (Dolby's default is on). --legacy-authoring makes a stream for older disc-authoring tools; such a stream carries no warp mode.

docs.title: Through dee_shim
docs.text: When DeeZy finds dee_shim, every thd-atmos encode runs through it, and a master of no more elements than --atmos-elements is coded as it is, so the stream decodes to it sample for sample. --no-as-is keeps DEE's own processing. --drc none needs dee_shim.

docs.title: Loudness and DRC
docs.text: DEE measures the loudness and writes the measured dialnorm; --custom-dialnorm writes a set one and --loudness-preset works as for Dolby Digital. --drc sets every presentation's DRC profile.

docs.title: Warp mode
docs.text: A TrueHD Atmos stream that carries no warp mode reaches DEE with none, which DEE renders as warping, its own default. --thd-warp-mode gives such a stream one (normal, warping, prologiciix or loro). A stream that has a warp mode keeps it. DeeZy 1.x gave every such stream normal. The warp mode changes no TrueHD audio, only the flag in the stream.

docs.title: Dolby TrueHD (thd)
docs.text:
Dolby TrueHD, lossless, written as .thd (.mlp is taken too). Every option is on deezy encode thd.

deezy encode thd movie.mkv
deezy encode thd --channels 8 --drc none movie.mkv

docs.title: Layouts and sample rate
docs.text:
--channels picks 2.0 (2), 5.1 (6) or 7.1 (8). Auto (0, the default) takes the smallest layout that holds every source channel and fills the rest with silence: a mono source becomes full-level dual mono, and a 5.0 or 7.0 source gets a silent LFE, as does --disable-lfe.

Use --layout 5.1.2 to preserve a source with side surrounds and front heights. It requires dee_shim and accepts --channels 0 (auto) or 8. The stream carries a 5.1.2 presentation plus 5.1 and stereo downmixes.

deezy encode thd --layout 5.1.2 input.wav

DEE encodes 48 or 96 kHz: a source above 48 kHz is encoded at 96 kHz, any other at 48 kHz.

--surround-3db lowers surround channels by 3 dB on multichannel encodes. It is off by default.

docs.title: Loudness and DRC
docs.text: DEE measures the loudness and writes the measured dialnorm; --custom-dialnorm writes a set one, and --loudness-preset works as for Dolby Digital. TrueHD is lossless, so nothing corrects the audio. --drc sets the DRC profile of every presentation in the stream (film_light by default); none needs dee_shim.

docs.title: Through dee_shim
docs.text: When DeeZy finds dee_shim, every thd encode runs through it. At 96 kHz dee_shim turns off DEE's apodizing filter, so the stream decodes to the source sample for sample; --no-as-is keeps DEE's filter.
